simple.meaning: אָכַף (ʼâkaph) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to urge.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Proverbs, beginning at Proverbs 16:26. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אָכַף (H404) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: אָכַף (ʼâkaph) / H404 is traced through Proverbs 16:26 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H404. akaph אָכַף verb press, urge (Mishna id. , Aramaic be urgent , compare , Arabic saddle ); — Qal Perfect Prov 16:26 ׳א מִּ֑יהוּ עָלָיו (|| לוֺ עָֽמְלָה עָמֵל נֶפֶשׁ ) i.e. his hunger impels him to work.
definitions.rootNote: a primitive root; apparently meaning to curve (as with a burden);

occurrences.englishText: The appetite of the laboring man labors for him;
